Laura — reviewed and attached annotated counsel comments (LA_redline_comments_v1.pdf). Summary of material points and recommended positions:

1) Subprocessors / notice period
- Customer asks for 30-day notice + opt-out for new subprocessors in healthcare workloads. Redwood position: 30-day notice is reasonable, but we cannot offer a contractual opt-out that blocks a subprocessor for general platform improvements. Proposed compromise: 30-day notice + right to object for specific categories (e.g., data hosting vs ancillary analytics) with good-faith escalation; if not resolved within 10 business days, default to Redwood's standard security posture.

2) EU->US transfers / SCCs
- They request SCCs + explicit addendum listing subprocessors. Counsel: Accept SCCs; provide an EU-US Transfer Addendum template and agree to provide an up-to-date subprocessor registry via a customer portal link (not in-line exhaustive list). For high-risk subprocessors (if any), offer an addendum annex on request.

3) Incident notification SLA
- 24-hour initial notification for material incidents is aggressive. Recommend 72-hour initial notification for incidents involving patient data, with same-day initial acknowledgement for confirmed incidents. Where possible, add an internal expedite channel for Clearwater's security ops.

4) Data deletion and return
- Clarify the deletion window post-termination: propose 60 days for customer-requested export + certified deletion.

5) Audit / evidence requests
- Provide SOC 2 Type II report and limited evidence via secure link. Resist on-site audits except for enterprise customers on dedicated/private plans; offer remote evidence review instead.

Suggested next steps (from counsel):
- Send a redline response accepting SCCs and notice period but pushing back on broad opt-out.
- Offer the EU-US addendum + subprocessor portal link.
- Propose 72-hour incident notification with expedited acknowledgement.

Attachment: LA_redline_comments_v1.pdf (pdf, 22KB)

I can draft redline language for the above if you want — call me later today and I will take a pass.

—Marcus
